body:
> This makes it necessary to press `<CTRL-O>` twice to go back to the previous cursor position

This is fairly common in Vim. Would be nice to fix it for more than just `:drop`.

~~Although, in your case it looks like the column differs between the jumps, so that's not exactly a "duplicate" jump.~~

> This is fairly common in Vim. Would be nice to fix it for more than just :drop.

Can you point me to any more general related issues? I'd like to see if I can tackle this one.

> Although, in your case it looks like the column differs between the jumps, so that's not exactly a "duplicate" jump.

Actually it's the same column, no further jumping movements are needed after `:drop` to reproduce this behavior. Both jumps refer to the first line and the first column.

> Can you point me to any more general related issues? I'd like to see if I can tackle this one.

I've been too lazy to track down minimal steps to reproduce the issue. But anyways, I think it's reasonable to never add duplicate adjacent jumps. So just preventing that should prevent all cases.

Based on recent Vim discussions about duplicate _undo_ steps, I wouldn't be surprised if duplicate _jump_ behavior is considered "the way Vi does it, therefore Vim must do it". But I think Neovim doesn't need to maintain such "compatibility": it won't break scripts (because (1) the behavior is nonsensical/undefined, and (2) Vim sometimes changes the behavior anyways ... thus this is purely _human_ interface, no scripts/plugins would depend on it).

body:
Following question on vi.stackexchange.com might be related to this:

https://vi.stackexchange.com/questions/19038/pressing-ctrl-o-twice-is-required-to-return-to-previous-entry-in-jumplist

> Following question on vi.stackexchange.com might be related to this:
> 
> https://vi.stackexchange.com/questions/19038/pressing-ctrl-o-twice-is-required-to-return-to-previous-entry-in-jumplist

Thanks a lot for your input. Just confirmed the issue mentioned in the link.
@justinmk <strike>This [one](https://vi.stackexchange.com/questions/19038/pressing-ctrl-o-twice-is-required-to-return-to-previous-entry-in-jumplist) will most probably require the fix you talked about</strike>

Did some debugging and I believe this is the offending line:
https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/master/src/nvim/main.c#L513

Same issue we had with `do_argfile`, while setting the pcmark in `main`, the call to `setpcmark` adds an entry to the jumplist for the current position, so we end up with something like this:
```
$ nvim -u NONE -i NONE
:jumps                                                                
 jump line  col file/text
   1     1    0                   <= this shouldn't be here
>
```

While we can simply replace the call with `setpcmark_ext(false)` as with the previous issue, but since there are around 46 `setpcmark` calls in the codebase I suspect we see other similar issues with the same cause, dunno how to tackle this more generally...

issue.title: Jumplist deletes jumps on the current line

labels.name: closed:wontfix
labels.description: current behavior is by design, and change is not desired

repository.name: neovim
repository.description: Vim-fork focused on extensibility and usability

issue.body:
- `nvim --version`: NVIM v0.4.0-1760-g7ed212262
- `vim -u DEFAULTS` (version: 8.0) behaves differently? yes
- Operating system/version: WIndows 10
- Terminal name/version: nvim-qt

Using :jumps, calling getjumplist() or using ctrl-o when the topmost jumplist entry is on the current line deletes that jumplist entry.

### Steps to reproduce using `nvim -u NORC`

- Generate a file for testing, e.g. `100ia<esc>yy5p`

Reproduction:
- Create a jumplist entry with m'
- Move somewhere else on the same line
- use ctrl-o

### Actual behaviour
We delete the jumplist entry on the current line and jump to some previous jumplist entry.

### Expected behaviour
Jump back to the marked location on the current line. Create a jump point in the location we used ctrl-o at which will replace the jumplist entry since we can only have one jumplist entry per line.
(Whether this behavior is intuitive is debatable but it's what vim and older neovim versions do)
